study_identification_part.si4_title: Contrasting Case-Control and Normative Reference Approaches to Capture Clinically Relevant Structural Brain Abnormalities in Patients With First-Episode Psychosis Who Are Antipsychotic Naive

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To evaluate whether baseline deviations from a normative reference range in subcortical volumes are better predictors of antipsychotic treatment response than raw volumes in patients with first-episode psychosis (FEP) who were naive to antipsychotic medication.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Associations with antipsychotic treatment response (16-week risperidone trial, flexible dosing; option to switch to aripiprazole for adverse effects) were examined using: (1) Partial correlations between raw volumes and treatment response (percentage improvement in positive symptoms), controlling for age and sex; (2) Pearson correlations between deviation z-scores and treatment response. Statistical comparison of correlation coefficients between raw volume and deviation measures was performed using Fisher's z-transformation (reported as z-statistics with p-values). Bonferroni corrections were applied for multiple comparisons in post hoc analyses. Results showed that deviation measures in caudate (z = -2.17; P = .03) and putamen (z = -2.15; P = .03) were significantly more predictive of treatment response compared to raw volumes. Negative deviations in caudate, putamen, and ventral diencephalon were associated with better treatment response, while raw volumes showed no significant associations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling revealed heterogeneous structural brain deviations in FEP patients (36% showed extreme deviations), and negative deviations in key dopaminergic regions (caudate, putamen, ventral diencephalon) were significantly better predictors of antipsychotic treatment response than raw volumes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: In case-control analyses, FEP patients (n=98) had significantly lower raw volumes in thalamus (F=9.63, P=.002), hippocampus (F=17.23, P=.009), amygdala (F=6.55, P=.01), ventral diencephalon (F=4.84, P=.03), and brainstem (F=8.39, P=.004) compared to controls (n=92). However, ventricle volumes did not differ between groups. Using normative modeling, 36% of FEP patients displayed extreme deviations (≥2 SD); 22% had extreme ventricle deviations and 22% had extreme subcortical deviations. Extreme deviations in subcortical regions were twice as likely to be negative rather than positive, while 62% of extreme ventricle deviations were positive. Critically, while raw subcortical volumes showed no association with 16-week antipsychotic treatment response, negative deviations in caudate, putamen, and ventral diencephalon were significantly associated with better response. Statistical comparisons confirmed that deviation measures were superior to raw volumes for predicting response in caudate (z=-2.17, P=.03) and putamen (z=-2.15, P=.03). These three regions are key dopaminergic areas, supporting the interpretation that negative structural deviations may reflect dopamine dysfunction that is reversible with antipsychotic treatment.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: This study demonstrates clinical utility of normative modeling in psychiatry by showing that individual deviations are more clinically relevant than group-level case-control differences. The findings suggest that negative deviations in dopaminergic regions (caudate, putamen, ventral diencephalon) may serve as predictive biomarkers for antipsychotic treatment response in FEP. The study enrolled a diverse sample with over 60% identifying as racial/ethnic minorities and achieved excellent retention (82%) in the 16-week medication trial. The heterogeneity revealed by normative modeling (e.g., 9% of patients showed extreme negative ventricle deviations, an unexpected finding) underscores the limitation of group-average approaches and the importance of individual-level characterization for precision psychiatry.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study did not exclude patients who used cannabis, which is a major risk factor for psychosis, though this was justified to maintain generalizability. The choice of covariates (age and sex) was made to be consistent between raw volume and deviation analyses, rather than using total intracranial volume for raw data (though results were unchanged when intracranial volume was used). The study focused on subcortical and ventricle regions only, not examining cortical structures. The specific mechanisms linking negative structural deviations in dopaminergic regions to treatment response remain speculative. The normative reference model's composition and characteristics are described in separate publications rather than fully detailed in this paper.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study represents an important application of normative modeling to demonstrate clinical utility in predicting treatment outcomes. The use of a large reference model (n=58,836) from brain charts and local calibration with site-specific controls (n=92) follows methodological best practices for transferring normative models to new sites. The study included antipsychotic-naive FEP patients, which is a significant strength as it avoids medication confounds. The finding that 9% of patients had extreme negative ventricle deviations is noted as an unexpected and poorly understood phenomenon not previously reported. Treatment consisted of risperidone on a flexible dosing scheme (mean dose 4.39±2.52 mg at week 16), with 4 patients switching to aripiprazole and 2 opting out of medication. Duration of untreated psychosis was relatively long (mean 23.60±40.15 months). The study's imaging protocol used high-resolution sequences (0.8 mm³ voxels) on a 3T Siemens Magnetom Prisma scanner. Race/ethnicity distribution in FEP group: African American 57.1%, White 37.8%, Asian <5%, with other groups each representing <5% of participants.
